욥기-13-4.exegesis: 3. Job wishes to plead his cause before God ( Job 9:34 , 35 ), as he is more and more convinced of the valueless character of his would-be "physicians" ( Job 16:2 ).

욥기-13-5.title: 욥기 13장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-5.exegesis: 4. forgers of lies-- literally, "artful twisters of vain speeches" [Umbreit].
욥기-13-5.theologicalNote: 4. forgers of lies-- literally, "artful twisters of vain speeches" [Umbreit].

욥기-13-6.title: 욥기 13장 6절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-6.exegesis: 5. ( Pr 17:28 ). The Arabs say, "The wise are dumb; silence is wisdom."
욥기-13-6.theologicalNote: 5. ( Pr 17:28 ). The Arabs say, "The wise are dumb; silence is wisdom."

욥기-13-7.exegesis: 5. ( Pr 17:28 ). The Arabs say, "The wise are dumb; silence is wisdom."

욥기-13-8.title: 욥기 13장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-8.exegesis: 7. deceitfully-- use fallacies to vindicate God in His dealings; as if the end justified the means. Their "deceitfulness" for God, against Job, was that they asserted he was a sinner, because he was a sufferer.
욥기-13-8.theologicalNote: 7. deceitfully-- use fallacies to vindicate God in His dealings; as if the end justified the means. Their "deceitfulness" for God, against Job, was that they asserted he was a sinner, because he was a sufferer.

욥기-13-9.title: 욥기 13장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-9.exegesis: 8. accept his person-- God's; that is, be partial for Him, as when a judge favors one party in a trial, because of personal considerations. contend for God-- namely, with fallacies and prepossessions against Job before judgment ( Jud 6:31 ). Partiality can never please the impartial God, nor the goodness of the cause excuse the unfairness of the arguments.

욥기-13-10.title: 욥기 13장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-10.exegesis: 9. Will the issue to you be good, when He searches out you and your arguments? Will you be regarded by Him as pure and disinterested? mock-- ( Ga 6:7 ). Rather, "Can you deceive Him as one man?" &c.
욥기-13-10.theologicalNote: 9. Will the issue to you be good, when He searches out you and your arguments? Will you be regarded by Him as pure and disinterested? mock-- ( Ga 6:7 ). Rather, "Can you deceive Him as one man?" &c.

욥기-13-11.title: 욥기 13장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-11.exegesis: 10. If ye do, though secretly, act partially. (See on Job 13:8 ; Psa 82:1 , 2). God can successfully vindicate His acts, and needs no fallacious argument of man.
욥기-13-11.theologicalNote: 10. If ye do, though secretly, act partially. (See on Job 13:8 ; Psa 82:1 , 2). God can successfully vindicate His acts, and needs no fallacious argument of man.

욥기-13-12.title: 욥기 13장 12절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-12.exegesis: 11. make you afraid?-- namely, of employing sophisms in His name ( Jr 10:7 , 10 ).
욥기-13-12.theologicalNote: 11. make you afraid?-- namely, of employing sophisms in His name ( Jr 10:7 , 10 ).

욥기-13-13.title: 욥기 13장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-13.exegesis: 12. remembrances-- "proverbial maxims," so called because well remembered. like unto ashes-- or, "parables of ashes"; the image of lightness and nothingness ( Is 44:20 ). bodies-- rather, "entrenchments"; those of clay, as opposed to those of stone, are easy to be destroyed; so the proverbs, behind which they entrench themselves, will not shelter them when God shall appear to reprove them for their injustice to Job.

욥기-13-14.title: 욥기 13장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-14.exegesis: 13. Job would wish to be spared their speeches, so as to speak out all his mind as to his wretchedness ( Job 13:14 ), happen what will.
욥기-13-14.theologicalNote: 13. Job would wish to be spared their speeches, so as to speak out all his mind as to his wretchedness ( Job 13:14 ), happen what will.

욥기-13-15.title: 욥기 13장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-15.exegesis: 14. A proverb for, "Why should I anxiously desire to save my life?" [Eichorn]. The image in the first clause is that of a wild beast, which in order to preserve his prey, carries it in his teeth. That in the second refers to men who hold in the hand what they want to keep secure.
욥기-13-15.theologicalNote: 14. A proverb for, "Why should I anxiously desire to save my life?" [Eichorn]. That in the second refers to men who hold in the hand what they want to keep secure.

욥기-13-16.title: 욥기 13장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-16.exegesis: 15. in him-- So the margin or keri, reads. But the textual reading or chetib is "not," which agrees best with the context, and other passages wherein he says he has no hope ( Job 6:11 ; 7:21 ; 10:20 ; 19:10 ). "Though He slay me, and I dare no more hope, yet I will maintain," &c., that is, "I desire to vindicate myself before Him," as not a hypocrite [Umbreit and Noyes].

욥기-13-17.title: 욥기 13장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-17.exegesis: 16. He-- rather, "This also already speaks in my behalf (literally, 'for my saving acquittal') for an hypocrite would not wish to come before Him" (as I do) [Umbreit]. (See last clause of Job 13:15 ).
욥기-13-17.theologicalNote: 16. He-- rather, "This also already speaks in my behalf (literally, 'for my saving acquittal') for an hypocrite would not wish to come before Him" (as I do) [Umbreit]. (See last clause of Job 13:15 ).

욥기-13-18.title: 욥기 13장 18절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-18.exegesis: 17. my declaration-- namely, that I wish to be permitted to justify myself immediately before God. with your ears-- that is, attentively.
욥기-13-18.theologicalNote: 17. my declaration-- namely, that I wish to be permitted to justify myself immediately before God. with your ears-- that is, attentively.

욥기-13-19.title: 욥기 13장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-19.exegesis: 18. ordered-- implying a constant preparation for defense in his confidence of innocence.
욥기-13-19.theologicalNote: 18. ordered-- implying a constant preparation for defense in his confidence of innocence.

욥기-13-20.title: 욥기 13장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-20.exegesis: 19. if, &c.-- Rather, "Then would I hold my tongue and give up the ghost"; that is, if any one can contend with me and prove me false, I have no more to say. "I will be silent and die." Like our "I would stake my life on it" [Umbreit].
욥기-13-20.theologicalNote: 19. if, &c.-- Rather, "Then would I hold my tongue and give up the ghost"; that is, if any one can contend with me and prove me false, I have no more to say. "I will be silent and die." Like our "I would stake my life on it" [Umbreit].

욥기-13-21.title: 욥기 13장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-21.exegesis: 20. Address to God. not hide-- stand forth boldly to maintain my cause.
욥기-13-21.theologicalNote: 20. Address to God. not hide-- stand forth boldly to maintain my cause.

욥기-13-23.title: 욥기 13장 23절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-23.exegesis: 22. call-- a challenge to the defendant to answer to the charges. answer-- the defense begun. speak-- as plaintiff. answer-- to the plea of the plaintiff. Expressions from a trial.
욥기-13-23.theologicalNote: 22. call-- a challenge to the defendant to answer to the charges. answer-- the defense begun. speak-- as plaintiff. answer-- to the plea of the plaintiff. Expressions from a trial.

욥기-13-24.title: 욥기 13장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-24.exegesis: 23. The catalogue of my sins ought to be great, to judge from the severity with which God ever anew crushes one already bowed down. Would that He would reckon them up! He then would see how much my calamities outnumber them. sin?-- singular, "I am unconscious of a single particular sin, much less many" [Umbreit].

욥기-13-25.title: 욥기 13장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-25.exegesis: 24. hidest ... face-- a figure from the gloomy impression caused by the sudden clouding over of the sun. enemy-- God treated Job as an enemy who must be robbed of power by ceaseless sufferings ( Job 7:17 , 21 ).
욥기-13-25.theologicalNote: 24. hidest ... face-- a figure from the gloomy impression caused by the sudden clouding over of the sun. enemy-- God treated Job as an enemy who must be robbed of power by ceaseless sufferings ( Job 7:17 , 21 ).

욥기-13-26.title: 욥기 13장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-26.exegesis: 25. ( Le 26:36 ; Psa 1:4 ). Job compares himself to a leaf already fallen, which the storm still chases hither and thither. break-- literally, "shake with (Thy) terrors." Jesus Christ does not "break the bruised reed" ( Is 42:3 , 27:8 ).

욥기-13-27.title: 욥기 13장 27절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-27.exegesis: 26. writest-- a judicial phrase, to note down the determined punishment. The sentence of the condemned used to be written down ( Is 10:1 ; Jr 22:30 ; Psa 149:9 ) [Umbreit]. bitter things-- bitter punishments. makest me to possess-- or "inherit." In old age he receives possession of the inheritance of sin thoughtlessly acquired in youth. "To inherit sins" is to inherit the punishments inseparably connected with them in Hebrew ideas ( Psa 25:7 ).

욥기-13-28.title: 욥기 13장 28절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-13-28.exegesis: 27. stocks-- in which the prisoner's feet were made fast until the time of execution ( Jr 20:2 ). lookest narrowly-- as an overseer would watch a prisoner. print-- Either the stocks, or his disease, marked his soles (Hebrew, "roots") as the bastinado would. Better, thou drawest (or diggest) [Gesenius] a line (or trench) [Gesenius] round my soles, beyond which I must not move [Umbreit].
